title: Engine heartbeat: the IDE tells a busy engine from a stuck one
summary: A running engine reports what it is doing, so the IDE kills only an engine whose status stopped moving
intro: Read this to understand why a long index or lint-all no longer gets killed while it works, and why a frozen engine still is. The engine keeps a status record (action, step, n of total) and answers it on a status-only pipe, drag-lint-beat-*, next to the control pipe. The IDE plugin polls it every two seconds: a changing record counts as progress, a frozen record on a spinning process counts as stuck. The status bar shows it, e.g. 'index parse 120/400'. An old engine or a verb without a beat falls back to the earlier output-or-CPU rule.
